items.tx:
If this week’s cyberattacks have shown us anything, it’s how absolutely necessary it is for the UK to have sovereign AI capabilities.

This is now urgent. 

In the past, the most sophisticated hacking and cyberattack work required considerable expertise, time, and resources. Nation states, intelligence agencies and rogue hacking groups had a substantial advantage - a tiny, tiny number of people.

Today, AI is able to rapidly identify these vulnerabilities, so it's much easier for hostile actors to point an AI at a certain piece of software and ask it to find potential exploits - including in the software that runs many of our key institutions across the public and private sectors.

It is absolutely conceivable that Britain’s hospitals, defence infrastructure, and national grid could be targeted in future cyberattacks. It's already being planned. If these were to be damaged or disabled as a result, thousands could die. If not more. 

It is therefore essential that we have the ability to defend ourselves - and the only way to do that is by developing AI sovereignty.

Cybersecurity, and actually much of the global economy, will increasingly rely on AI. It will be an essential tool in combating these sophisticated cyberattacks, alongside skilled people and secure domestic infrastructure.

As things stand, the dominant players are the US and China, but Britain is well positioned to become a serious third force in AI development.

Outside the EU, we have the freedom to set our own domestic regulatory framework, and we could have some of the cheapest energy in the world if we implemented Restore Britain’s energy security strategy.

We cannot afford to be beholden to a foreign power for any of the essentials of life.

Food, energy, defence and, increasingly, AI.

We must build our own infrastructure and train our own models. We must equip our people with the skills to build this industry. Electricians, plumbers, construction workers, and software engineers.

Done right, it can bring benefits to our people, but more importantly - the steps outlined here are absolutely essential for our national security.

items.tx:
JAMENI NAIROBI TULIKOSEA MUNGU WAPI? 

The people of Nairobi need change. They need responsible leadership, accountability, and a government that values human life. Today, a 14-storey building collapsed in Eastleigh, leaving several people trapped inside. My prayers are with the families, friends, and relatives of those trapped inside, and I hope for their safe rescue. This tragedy raises serious concerns about corruption, impunity, and failures within City Hall’s planning and construction oversight departments. When buildings collapse and lives are endangered without meaningful action, it demonstrates a failure of leadership and a government that is not adequately protecting its people.

When I was serving in the Environment Department, I tried to stop illegal construction activities involving excavation from one beacon to another. My efforts were met with hostility from my former boss, who summoned the entire City Hall government to a meeting at Charter Hall. Those present included CECs, County Chief Officers, Sub-County Administrators, Ward Administrators, all Environment Officers and his handlers . 

During that meeting, two innocent Environment Officers were suspended for carrying out their professional duties of stopping an illegal excavation at Roysambu Subcounty and south C . A few months later, a building collapsed in South C, killing three people. I have evidence relating to these events, and I am prepared to present it through the appropriate channels.

I was warned to keep off construction sites and even instructed not to undertake environmental work that required the involvement of our technical experts. This raises serious questions about whether professionals are being allowed to perform their duties independently and whether public safety is being sacrificed to protect other interests.

Developers in Nairobi have also raised serious concerns about the approval process. I have information alleging that some developers spend millions of shillings to obtain building approvals, with figures reportedly reaching at least KSh 56 million and, in the case of some foreign developers Chinese and others, KSh 92 million or more. These allegations must be independently investigated, and anyone found engaging in corruption must be held accountable. 

The approval of buildings must be guided by qualified professionals, technical assessments, and strict compliance with safety standards not political influence. No single individual should override the professional judgment of experts when the lives of Nairobi residents are at stake.

I therefore appeal to His Excellency the President to intervene and help restore order and accountability in Nairobi’s construction sector, including by ensuring that qualified experts from the national government support independent investigations and the enforcement of building safety regulations.

I am also aware of threats and intimidation against me. I have already recorded a statement with the police concerning two politicians whom I have implicated, and I intend to record a further statement at DCI Headquarters. I call upon the relevant security agencies to investigate these concerns and ensure my safety, as well as the safety of everyone who dares to speak out against wrongdoing.

Nairobi needs fair politics not corruption, intimidation, or the loss of innocent lives.

Our people deserve leadership that protects them. Our professionals deserve the freedom to do their jobs without fear. Our developers deserve a transparent and fair approval process. Above all, every Nairobi resident deserves to live and work in a city where human life is valued above money and political interests.

Nairobi needs change. Nairobi needs accountability. Nairobi deserves leadership that puts people first.

When they hear the war drums beating that Dems are going to ransack Texas, they immediately become the most “high prop” voters there are.

150,000 brand new R votes every 2 years is enough to cancel out and margin erosion in suburban counties and sponge up Travis/Dallas.

Plain old chalkboard math is as valid in election analysis as anything else.

October 23, 1983. A date forever etched in the hearts of United States Marines.

Forty-three years ago, a terrorist drove a truck loaded with explosives into the Marine barracks in Beirut, Lebanon, killing 241 American service members, including 220 Marines, 18 sailors, and 3 soldiers.

They were sons, brothers, husbands, fathers, and friends. Young Americans who had answered their country’s call, never knowing they would never see home again.

For those of us who have worn the Eagle, Globe, and Anchor, Beirut is not just another tragic event in American history. Those were our brothers. We may never have met them, but we share a bond that neither time nor death can break.

Forty-three years have passed. Families have grown older, children have grown up without their fathers, and parents have gone to their graves still mourning their sons.

But I promise you one thing. The United States Marine Corps has not forgotten them, and we never will.

Rest peacefully, brothers. Your sacrifice will never be forgotten.

Semper Fidelis. Always Faithful.

We also visited Auschwitz together. Standing there, surrounded by the evidence of unimaginable crimes, one truth became painfully clear: “Never again” must never become an empty slogan. We cannot honor the victims of yesterday while turning our backs on those facing atrocities today.

And our solidarity must cross borders.

I have also invited a woman from Africa to stand alongside the women of Iran and Afghanistan, to remind the world that sexual violence is still being used as a weapon of war and repression. Different countries, different forms of brutality, but one shared struggle for dignity, equality, and freedom.

We cannot expect women facing prison, bullets, acid attacks, rape, and execution to defeat these systems of oppression with their bare hands while the rest of the world stands aside.

And here is my message to the world:

South Africa’s apartheid did not fall because its victims fought alone. It fell because courageous people inside the country resisted, and the world joined their struggle.

In the history Poland gave the world Solidarność. Now the women of Iran Afghanistan and Africa need the world to live up to that word.

If the world could unite to help end racial apartheid in South Africa, and end tyranny in Poland, it can unite to end dictatorship everywhere. 

The time for solidarity is not after the atrocities. It is NOW.

items.tx:
Some people speak without knowing or understanding the true situation...

Yemen has been at war since 2015, enduring immense suffering and heavy bombardment. We lived not just for days, but for months without electricity, gasoline, or gas.

Bombs rained down on us daily. Our airports and ports were closed. We were attacked from all sides. We lived through incredibly difficult times.

Thanks be to God, we were able to endure everything. We adapted to the war, the fighting, and the bombing. The war itself became less of a hardship than the siege. The longer the siege lasted, the more difficult our situation became. Every passing year was harder than the last. Then a truce and negotiations took place, and the siege eased slightly... it didn't end, it just lessened.

Not a year passed before the events in Gaza began. Although our wounds were still raw, we hadn't even begun to heal when we entered a war with Israel, America, and Britain. The bombing resumed, and worse still, the siege intensified.

Immense suffering. A major war, a suffocating siege, our situation is unenviable due to the accumulation of suffering, problems, and the dire humanitarian situation.

We are the people most in need of respite, rest, peace, and time to heal our wounds. We are the most oppressed people, having endured immense suffering. We are the people who least want war and who most strive to avoid any problems, fighting, or wars.

We are not fighting this war with Saudi Arabia because we want to, but because we are forced to. We are compelled because we have no other choice. The world will continue to watch us die from disease and poverty. No one will have mercy on us, and even those who do will be powerless to help us.

...

This war was imposed upon us against our will. This war is our only hope to end the injustice and suffering inflicted upon us. We will not accept half-measures, we will not accept any truce, we will not accept a peace in which we die under siege...

There is no easy path for us to take. It is either a path of fighting and sacrifice, where we seize our rights and freedom, or a path of siege and starvation, where we await the mercy of our enemy while we slowly die.

After Chinese incursions, the people of Arunachal Pradesh now face violence from their own government.

The BJP government’s proposed 11,000 MW mega dam in the Siang Valley threatens to submerge at least 27 Adi villages and displace thousands.

For the Adi tribe, the Siang is Ane Siang – Mother Siang. The project threatens their ancestral lands, homes, wet-rice fields, traditional diets, indigenous knowledge and sacred bond with the river.

Worse, pre-feasibility surveys and drilling are reportedly being pushed ahead without the free, prior and informed consent of traditional village councils (Kebang), amid the deployment of central security forces.

The environmental risks are equally grave. Located in Seismic Zone V, the region faces serious earthquake, landslide, flash-flood and potentially catastrophic dam-failure risks, threatening communities across Arunachal Pradesh and downstream Assam.

The BJP’s message to Arunachal Pradesh is clear: your concerns will be ignored, your consent bypassed and your protests met with force.

This is Modi’s North-East policy in action: stepmotherly treatment.
